A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRDF research and provide complete, readable main text and Appendix A. All 18 tables, five figures, and Algorithm 1 can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SRDF navigation and instruction-generation results, ablations, and qualitative examples in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original SRDF experiments and outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix A, including benchmark comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same generator–navigator refinement procedure, Mantis and DUET components, decoding strategies, and filtering thresholds. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both use the same MP3D/HM3D training coverage and evaluate R2R, RxR-English, CVDN, REVERIE, SOON, R4R, and R2R-CE, plus instruction generation. The appendix's outdoor and OCR examples are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the navigation, instruction-generation, filtering, and appendix comparisons. The added Tan et al. citation does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendices A.1, A.4, and A.5 retain identical splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, sample sizes, and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The filtering, instruction-diversity, environment-scaling, fourth-round, alternative-MLLM, and encoding-format analyses are unchanged. Appendix A.7 retains the same qualitative case studies.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without random-seed details, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical result entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, both report 78% R2R test SPL in Table 7 and 26.2 SPICE for the final instruction generator in Table 9; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical notation, data-subset definitions, and iterative updates in Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about automatic mutual refinement, SRDF-20M, surpassing human R2R SPL, scalability, and transfer across navigation tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning instruction quality, directional alignment, filtering reliability, transferability, and qualitative capabilities are identical. No applicability boundary or substantive limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 retain the same hyperparameters, initialization, LoRA configuration, hardware, and training details. The code and data availability statement is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Tan et al. (2024), Large language models for data annotation and synthesis: A survey, to the dataset-curation discussion and bibliography. Existing references and substantive research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The running header changes from Preprint to Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Apart from the added citation, prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer publication header and added citation/reference produce limited text reflow, including bibliography layout changes on pages 17–19. All figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds one survey citation and updates publication metadata, while retaining identical methods, experiments, results, explanations, and reproducibility information throughout the main text and appendix. These limited bibliographic and presentation edits produce no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
